market_question: Will Marco Rubio win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: A generic candidate this far out typically has single-digit chances of winning the presidency. Even assuming Rubio is a top Republican contender, the probability of winning both the nomination and the general election is likely around 5-8%. The market's 14.2% implied probability appears too high, suggesting an overvaluation of his chances.
evidence_points: Historical baseline for any named candidate four years before election is low single digits.
Rubio faces a crowded Republican field with strong potential rivals (e.g., DeSantis) and is not a clear frontrunner.
Implied probability from betting markets on similar long-shot candidates is typically much lower; 14.2% corresponds to roughly 6/1 odds, which is too short.
